key_insight: DICE co-evolves teacher and student interatomic potentials, using fast student-driven exploration and reliability-aware labelling to reduce development cost and teacher-error propagation.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a more efficient route to compact interatomic potentials for simulations of ceramics, solid electrolytes and metal–organic frameworks.
method: Use a fast student potential to explore atomic configurations.
Route high-support configurations to teacher labelling and low-support configurations to DFT using representation-based support assessment.
Alternate teacher and student updates rather than following a fixed two-stage distillation sequence.
evidence_signal: Across Al2O3, yttria-stabilised zirconia and MIL-120(Al), DICE used 140–494 target DFT reference configurations per system, with recorded student exploration times at 2.6–5.1% of corresponding teacher-driven estimates.
watch_item: Support assessment must reliably flag unfamiliar configurations; exploration-time savings alone do not establish equivalent reductions in total development cost.
paper_title: Accelerating interatomic potential development through student-driven exploration and reliability-aware distillation
